original_question: Let (M, g) be a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold, let p be a point of M, and let h be the pullback of g to the tangent space T_pM along the exponential map exp_p: T_pM -> M, allowing h to degenerate where exp_p fails to be regular. Does the possibly degenerate tensor h determine the pointed manifold (M, g, p) uniquely up to isometry?
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost verbatim: it has the exact hypotheses of a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold and a base point p, defines h as the pullback of g along the exponential map exp_p, explicitly allows h to degenerate where exp_p is singular, and asks the same reconstruction question of whether this data determines the manifold together with the base point up to isometry.
missing_details: To make the conclusion fully precise and stand-alone, the uniqueness should be stated for the pointed manifold (M,g,p), i.e. up to an isometry carrying p to the corresponding base point.

To compare the tensors coming from two different manifolds, one should specify that the comparison is made after a linear identification of the tangent spaces T_pM and T_{p'}M'; equivalently, if L:T_pM->T_{p'}M' is a linear isomorphism, then L^*(exp_{p'}^*g')=exp_p^*g.
It is helpful to spell out h explicitly as the possibly degenerate symmetric 2-tensor h_v(ξ,η)=g_{exp_p(v)}((d exp_p)_v ξ,(d exp_p)_v η).

The paper does not impose any extra dimension, analyticity, or genericity assumptions in the problem itself; those appear only as known affirmative special cases and should not be folded into the question.
refined_question: Let (M,g) be a simply connected complete Riemannian manifold and let p∈M. Define the symmetric 2-tensor h=exp_p^*g on T_pM by h_v(ξ,η)=g_{exp_p(v)}((d exp_p)_v ξ,(d exp_p)_v η); in general h may be degenerate at points v where d exp_p is singular. If (M',g',p') is another simply connected complete Riemannian manifold and there exists a linear isomorphism L:T_pM→T_{p'}M' such that L^*(exp_{p'}^*g')=exp_p^*g, must there exist an isometry F:(M,g)→(M',g') with F(p)=p'? Equivalently, does the possibly degenerate tensor h determine the pointed manifold (M,g,p) up to pointed isometry?
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Petrunin's Section 16, explicitly titled "Ambrose problem." The paper's formulation is essentially the same question: whether the pullback of the metric tensor to the tangent space via the exponential map at a base point determines the manifold and the base point up to isometry. The only sharpening needed is to make explicit the comparison of such tensors across different manifolds via a linear identification of tangent spaces and to phrase the conclusion as pointed isometry. The adjacent sentence in the paper also confirms the intended scope: no extra restrictions are part of the problem statement itself, while dimension 2, analytic metrics, and generic metrics are listed only as known cases with affirmative answers.
